question: Can precommitted coordinate Hensel steps raise the p-adic depth of one fresh public relation residual, and how does the exact rational height grow?
generator_law: first finite point by ascending x then y whose cofactor multiple has exact prime order q
query_law: first 16 lexicographic ordered distinct offsets with both U=Q-t1G and V=Q-t2G nonidentity
hit_selection: first public relation hit in field, target, query, vector order with distinct x coordinates; enumerate all 512 queries and 6656 vector tests to certify order
step_rule: for k=1..7, with current depth at least k, compute t(R) mod p^(k+1); if already zero mod p^(k+1) make no shift; else test coordinate axes x1,y1,x2,y2 in order by adding p^k once, choose first nonzero derivative d=(t1-t0)/p^k mod p, set delta=-((t0/p^k) mod p)/d mod p, and add p^(k-1)*delta to that shift coordinate
candidate_law: center U,V coordinates; add p times each integer shift; interpolate A=(f1-f2)/(x1-x2), B=f1-A*x1; require integral coefficient reduction and nonsingular curve
modular_residual: compute R=aP1+bP2 with Jacobian arithmetic modulo p^(k+1), t=-X*Z/Y in the reduction kernel; record failure if normal form or unit check fails
exact_controls: after each accepted step, construct rational curve and both points, compute exact R, record full rational coordinates, formal parameter numerator/denominator, p-adic depth and bit heights; independently replay every probe and step using Fraction group arithmetic
stop_rule: stop at exact rational relation, derivative exhaustion, invalid model, modular normal-form failure, exact mismatch, cap, or depth 8; retain all attempted axes and statuses
claim_boundary: one preselected fresh public hit is an existence/control experiment, not a relation-yield estimate; finite p-adic depth is not exact rational equality; compare rational height with depth; no same-target IC/rho speedup claim
